literal_meaning: Pouring oil into fire.
figurative_meaning: Making a bad situation worse by adding fuel to it.
example: Avaru vaadikkunnu, nee koodi parayanda — agnikku enna ozhikkuka.

literal_meaning: Child is in the armpit, but searching the entire town.
figurative_meaning: Looking for something that is right in front of you.
example: Chaabi kayyil undo, vazhi thedi nadakkunnu — kakshatthil kunju, ooru thedi.

literal_meaning: One stick for an elephant, the same stick for a goat.
figurative_meaning: Applying the same standard or punishment regardless of size or severity.
example: Chinna thettinaum valiya thettinaum oru shiksha — aanaakkorru dand.

literal_meaning: Nothing at home, yet giving away on the road.
figurative_meaning: Being generous to strangers while neglecting one's own family or responsibilities.
example: Swantham kutumbam panji, avaraanu sahaayikkunnathu — veettil illa vazhikku kodukkunnnu.

literal_meaning: A cannon to kill a mosquito.
figurative_meaning: Using a completely disproportionate response for a small problem.
example: Chinna prasnakku ithu valiya shiksha — kothukinne kollan peeranki.

literal_meaning: He who eats salt will drink water.
figurative_meaning: Every action has a corresponding consequence.
example: Kettaathu cheythu, ippol shikshaanubhavikkunnu — uppu thinnavan vellam kudikkum.

literal_meaning: A thief runs when he sees another thief.
figurative_meaning: A guilty person panics when they encounter someone who knows the truth.
example: Avan peru kettathu maatramennil ottham thudangi — kallane kandal kallan odum.

literal_meaning: Only the elephant knows elephant matters.
figurative_meaning: Only the person going through a situation truly understands it.
example: Ninakk enthariyo? Aval kashtam aval maathram ariyum — anaakkaaryam anaykku ariyaam.

literal_meaning: You cannot clap with one hand.
figurative_meaning: A conflict or collaboration requires both parties.
example: Randhu perkkaum thetti pattittundu — oru kai kondu kaiyatikkilla.

literal_meaning: He who climbs a tree must come down one day.
figurative_meaning: No one can stay at the top forever; pride before a fall.
example: Avan ippo valiyavan, pakshe kaalam maarum — maram keriyavan orunaal irangunm.

literal_meaning: Who will bell the cat?
figurative_meaning: Who will dare to do the risky task that everyone agrees needs to be done?
example: Managerod parayaan aarum thayaar aakkunilla — poochakku aaru mani kettum.

literal_meaning: The one who has nothing criticizes the one who has.
figurative_meaning: Envious people tend to criticize those who are more successful.
example: Avan vallathe cheyyunnavareyaanu vimarshikkunnathu — illaathavan ullavane aakshepikkum.

literal_meaning: Don't become a blacksmith just because you went to Kollam.
figurative_meaning: Don't pretend to be an expert just because of superficial exposure.
example: Oru class eduthu expert aayathupole parayunnu — kollatthu chennu kollar aakkaruthu.

literal_meaning: A bull that ran and a bull that runs.
figurative_meaning: Past and present mistakes are the same; same person repeating errors.
example: Athu cheythathum ithu cheythathum avan thanne — odiya kaala, odunna kaala.

literal_meaning: Work for the skilled, begging for the unskilled.
figurative_meaning: Skills determine your livelihood and dignity.
example: Padikkathe, yonum ellaathe irikkunnathu irappin samamaanu — thozhil ullavannu thozhil.

literal_meaning: A thorn removed by a thorn.
figurative_meaning: Fighting fire with fire; using similar means to counter a problem.
example: Avante thandhathinnu avanodu thanne yerichal mathi — kandakan kandakanaall.

literal_meaning: One must form habits while still a child.
figurative_meaning: Good habits must be cultivated from a young age.
example: Kallattu padippikkanam — unni aakumbol sheelikkkanam.

literal_meaning: One who has been drenched in rain does not fear dew.
figurative_meaning: Someone who has faced great hardship fears nothing lesser.
example: Aval itreyum kashtam kandathaanu — mazha nananjavan manju bhayakkilla.

literal_meaning: Crowing together in a flock does not help.
figurative_meaning: Collective noise without action or unity of purpose achieves nothing.
example: Ellaarum parayunnu pakshe arum cheyyunilla — koottatthode kooviyaal phalamill.

literal_meaning: One person will poke the other's eye.
figurative_meaning: People will harm those closest to them out of jealousy or rivalry.
example: Avaru koode pani cheythavaraanenkilum ippo thaanaarunnu — oruthan oruttante kannu kuttum.

literal_meaning: Once across the river, the boat is forgotten.
figurative_meaning: People forget those who helped them once they no longer need them.
example: Nee sahaayichu, pakshe kaaryam kazhinju avan manasillaathaayi — puzha kadannaal thoni marakkum.

literal_meaning: Lightning does not strike the same place twice.
figurative_meaning: The same misfortune rarely happens to the same person twice.
example: Oru thaval pizhachu, ippol sheriyaakunnu — idiminnall ore dikkil veezhill.

literal_meaning: Hope every week, disappointment every day.
figurative_meaning: Constant unfulfilled expectations leading to chronic disappointment.
example: Avante kezhill enna kaanikkunathu innum varunnilla — aazhchathorum aasha.

literal_meaning: The distant mountain always looks green.
figurative_meaning: Things appear better from a distance than up close.
example: Aavide nalla sthalamanu ennu thonn, pakshe povumbol ariyum — doorey ulla malakku pachapp.

literal_meaning: The desire for jackfruit starts when it's still at the root.
figurative_meaning: Craving or planning for something prematurely before it is ready.
example: Result varathe munp party cheyyaan plan idaruthu — chakka veril thodumbool kothi.

literal_meaning: One tree does not make a forest.
figurative_meaning: One person alone cannot create a major change or movement.
example: Oru aalinu maatram ithellam cheyyaan kazhiyill — otta vruksham kondu kaadaavilla.

literal_meaning: Boat in the sea, God alongside.
figurative_meaning: When in danger, one can only hope and trust in a higher power.
example: Paristhithi kayyil aalla, dhaivam thanne sahaaykkanam — kadalil thoni dhaivam koode.

literal_meaning: Small age, small wisdom.
figurative_meaning: Young people lack the experience to make wise decisions.
example: Avanu ithinte gurutharam ariyilla — cheriya praayattil cheriya buddhi.

literal_meaning: A tit-for-tat answer.
figurative_meaning: Giving a sharp, fitting counter-reply to a remark.
example: Avan ketti parayumbol aval udan madi parayum — urulakkupperi uttaram.

literal_meaning: The one who is with you is your companion.
figurative_meaning: Those who stand by you in difficult times are your true allies.
example: Kashtakaalatthu koode nillu ennal koode ullavan koottali.

literal_meaning: Deceit will work only once.
figurative_meaning: You can fool someone only once; repeated deception fails.
example: Avan innum try cheyyunnu, pakshe aarum vishwasikkyunilla — kalltharam orikkal phalikkum.

literal_meaning: A fish that joins the current.
figurative_meaning: Someone who simply goes along with whatever is happening without independent thought.
example: Aval swaathanthrya abhipraayam illathe ellaarum parayunnapole cheyyunnu — ozhukil cherunna meen.

literal_meaning: Where there is hope, there is life.
figurative_meaning: Hope is what keeps a person going through hardship.
example: Nirashapedathe — aasha ullidelttholam jeevan.

literal_meaning: Double result requires double effort.
figurative_meaning: Greater rewards demand greater work.
example: Nannaayi cheythaal nannaayi kitum — iratti phalam iratti adhvaanam.

literal_meaning: Speak the truth so the heart feels cool.
figurative_meaning: Expressing the truth brings inner peace.
example: Marikkaathe parayoo — ullath parayunnathu ullam kulirkkum.

literal_meaning: Leaves fall, but the tree stands.
figurative_meaning: Individuals come and go but the institution or family remains.
example: Aarum permanent alla, organization nilkkum — kozhinjupokum ila, pakhe maram nilkkum.

literal_meaning: One hardship a day.
figurative_meaning: Life brings a new challenge every day; trouble is relentless.
example: Innale onnu, innale mattonnu — oru divasam oru kashtam.

literal_meaning: Remember while you still can remember.
figurative_meaning: Do not take things or people for granted; appreciate while you still have them.
example: Avarul koode ullappol madikkoo — orma ullappol orkkkanam.

literal_meaning: The sun rises and the sun sets.
figurative_meaning: Everything has a beginning and an end; no situation lasts forever.
example: Ithum maari pookum — njayar udikkyum, njayar asthamikkyum.

literal_meaning: Do not put down a burden you have taken up.
figurative_meaning: Once you take on a responsibility, see it through.
example: Nee accept cheythathinu maarum parayaruthu — etta bhaaram irakkkaruthu.

literal_meaning: Two oarsmen in one boat.
figurative_meaning: Having two leaders or decision-makers causes conflict and inefficiency.
example: Randhu managersund, karyam nadakkunilla — oru vallattil randu thandu kaar.

literal_meaning: If there is food, eat; if not, sleep.
figurative_meaning: Accept what life gives you without complaining.
example: Muzhuvanum kittiyilla, kazhinjathe kond santhushtan aakoo — undenghil unnu, illenghil urakkoo.

literal_meaning: If a crow bathes, will it become an egret?
figurative_meaning: External changes cannot alter one's true nature.
example: Avan dress maatti, swabhavam maatti — kaakka kulichu kondakku aakumo.

literal_meaning: Give what is craved, and also what is not liked.
figurative_meaning: Life gives you what you want and also what you don't want.
example: Nallathu varumbol kettathum varaam — kothichathu kodukkkanam, ishtapadaathathum.

literal_meaning: What is today may not be tomorrow.
figurative_meaning: Wealth, power, and circumstances are impermanent.
example: Ippol nalla kaalamu, pakshe marappikkanda — innu ullath naale illa.

literal_meaning: A running horse doesn't need a whip.
figurative_meaning: A motivated and capable person needs no external push.
example: Avan sradhayulla aal, parayanda — odunna kuthirakku chaattavaar venda.

literal_meaning: A rolling stone gathers no moss.
figurative_meaning: A person who keeps moving never settles or accumulates anything.
example: Avan oru stalathu nilkkarunilla — urunda kallu paayal pidikkila.

literal_meaning: The thief who is with you.
figurative_meaning: An enemy within your trusted circle is the most dangerous.
example: Avane viswasichu, avan thanne kettathi — koode ulla kallan.

literal_meaning: Time is medicine.
figurative_meaning: Time heals all wounds.
example: Ippol vedanikkunu, pakshe kaalam cheyyum — kaalam aushadham.

literal_meaning: If you have ten coins, you have ten virtues.
figurative_meaning: Wealth is perceived as a substitute for good character; money changes how people are treated.
example: Avanu panam aayappazhal ellaarum mechunnu — panam pattum undenghil gunam pattum.

literal_meaning: Ran first, then walked.
figurative_meaning: Starting with great enthusiasm but losing momentum over time.
example: Prashikkum munnpu valiya utsaham, pinne vittu — aadyam odi pinne nadannu.

idiom: കള്ളം പറഞ്ഞ് ജീവിക്കാം, പക്ഷേ ഒരിക്കൽ മതി
literal_meaning: You can live by lying, but only once.
figurative_meaning: Deception may work once but eventually fails.
example: Vaaka onnu parayaam, pinne aarum vishwaasikkyukayilla — kallam parayunnathu orikkal mathi.

literal_meaning: The one who works will eat.
figurative_meaning: Only those who put in effort will receive their reward.
example: Padam padikkaathe expect cheyyanda — jaoli cheyyunavan bhakshanam kazhikkum.

literal_meaning: Two roosters in one cage.
figurative_meaning: Two dominant people cannot coexist in the same space without conflict.
example: Oru team il rendhu leaders — oru koottil randu pooovan.

literal_meaning: Do what you say, don't say what you have done.
figurative_meaning: Be a person of action and quiet deeds, not empty words.
example: Nee cheyyunnathu cheyyu, paranjukaanikkaruthu — paranjathu cheyyuka cheythatu parayaatirikkuka.

literal_meaning: Know the depth of the sea before you descend.
figurative_meaning: Understand the risks before committing to something.
example: Business start cheyyunmunnp research cheyyuka — kadalaazhum arhinju iranganam.

literal_meaning: The one with energy will eat.
figurative_meaning: The active and driven person will always find a way to survive and thrive.
example: Parisramikkan madicha vaadu eppozhum pinja — ooorjam ullavan unnum.

literal_meaning: A true friend struggles with you in your time of pain.
figurative_meaning: Real friendship means being there during hardship, not just in good times.
example: Kashtam vandappazhal koode nillu — utta changaathi uzhalum neram.

literal_meaning: Even if the sky falls, the mother is still the sky.
figurative_meaning: A mother's love and importance is irreplaceable no matter what.
example: Aval enne vittu poyalum amma enna feeling marailla — aakaasham idihnjalum amma aakaasham.

literal_meaning: One problem has a thousand solutions.
figurative_meaning: There is always more than one way to solve a difficulty.
example: Haaraatiriku, vaere vazhikal und — oru prashnatthinu aayiram uttaram.

literal_meaning: A big person will not do small work.
figurative_meaning: People with status or pride avoid tasks they consider beneath them, even when necessary.
example: Vaadu swaymam ceyyanam enghilum manikku — valiya aal cheriya jaoli cheyyilla.

literal_meaning: Do good and good will come to you.
figurative_meaning: Kindness and virtue are rewarded in return.
example: Sahaaayam cheythu, ippol avaru sahaayikkunnu — nallath cheythaal nallath labhikkum.

idiom: ഉടലിൽ ഒരു ജീവൻ, ഉള്ളിൽ ഒരു ഭയം
literal_meaning: One life in the body, one fear inside.
figurative_meaning: A person who has done wrong lives in constant fear of being exposed.
example: Avanu pazhaya vishayam manasilund — uddalil oru jeevan ullil oru bhayam.

literal_meaning: Mountains may move but the mind will not.
figurative_meaning: A stubborn person will not change their thinking no matter what.
example: Pala pravashyam parayunnu kaaryam illa — malakal neengum manassu neengilla.

literal_meaning: What existed yesterday does not exist today.
figurative_meaning: Nothing is permanent; circumstances change constantly.
example: Avarudey power ippo poyirikkunnu — innale undaayirunnathu innu illa.

literal_meaning: The one who starts with one will win in the end.
figurative_meaning: Persistent consistent effort leads to eventual success.
example: Pokaruthu, thudarnnu parishramichu — ondil thudanghiyavan oduiil jayikkum.

literal_meaning: Fruit before the leaf.
figurative_meaning: Getting results before putting in the proper foundation or process.
example: Training kazhiyathe projects ettedukkunnu — ilaykku munnne kaay.

literal_meaning: Where there is a person, there will be a crowd.
figurative_meaning: Success and good character attract people naturally.
example: Vaadu jelichittundu, anekam perum koode und — aal ullideltthu aalkkootam.

literal_meaning: Saw the left omen and broke.
figurative_meaning: Giving up at the first sign of bad luck or difficulty.
example: Oru failure konddu prashnikku angeer aadukayilla — idanger kandu odinnu.

literal_meaning: Eyes that have seen will close.
figurative_meaning: A witness who has seen too much will eventually be silenced.
example: Avanu sahshyam und kabaali — kanda kannu poottum.

literal_meaning: Flowing water causes no harm.
figurative_meaning: A person who keeps moving and adapts does not stagnate or become corrupted.
example: Adaptable aayirikkanam — ozhukkunna vellam dosham cheyyilla.

literal_meaning: One must study during the time for studying.
figurative_meaning: Every phase of life has its proper activity; missing the right time is costly.
example: Ippo padikkanam, pinne kaalam millaa — padikkkunna kaalatthu padikkanam.

literal_meaning: One life, only once.
figurative_meaning: Life is short and must not be wasted; make the most of every opportunity.
example: Chance vittu kalyanda — ore oru jeevan orikkal maathram.

literal_meaning: The earth revolves, the person stands still.
figurative_meaning: The world keeps changing and moving, but stubborn people refuse to adapt.
example: Ellaam maarunnu, avan maaranilla — bhoomi chuttunnu aal nilkkunnu.

literal_meaning: Reach out your hand and you will receive.
figurative_meaning: You must take initiative; opportunities come to those who try.
example: Request cheyyaathu dorakilla — kai neettiyaal kittum.

literal_meaning: If one person runs, a whole village runs.
figurative_meaning: Panic is contagious; one person's fear can spread to many.
example: Vaadu bhayann, pinne ellaarum bhayann — oraal odiyaal oru naadu odum.

literal_meaning: Double sorrow gives double strength.
figurative_meaning: Great suffering can build great resilience.
example: Avalu kashtatthil aayi, ippol avalu strong aanu — iratti dukham iratti balam.

literal_meaning: Everyone will be needed by someone at some point.
figurative_meaning: Never look down on anyone; everyone has value and use.
example: Avane angatth kaanaruthu — aarkum aarkum aavashyamaakum.

literal_meaning: One struck by lightning does not fear the wind.
figurative_meaning: Someone who has survived great hardship is not intimidated by lesser difficulties.
example: Aval ithreyum kashtam kanditund — idi vettiyavan kaatine bhayakkilla.

literal_meaning: One word, a thousand wars.
figurative_meaning: A single careless word can cause enormous conflict.
example: Avanu thettaayoru vakku parayaan, randham verupaadu undaayi — oru vaakku aayiram yuddham.

literal_meaning: Small rain, big mud.
figurative_meaning: A small event can cause disproportionately large problems.
example: Chinna prashnakku oru peddha vazhakk — cheriya mazha valiya chali.

literal_meaning: The giver is God.
figurative_meaning: A generous person is the most valued and respected in any community.
example: Avan ellaarum help cheyyunnu, anneyallaa avanre peru — kodukkunavan daivam.

literal_meaning: Medicine offered by one who already betrayed the goat.
figurative_meaning: A hypocritical remedy offered by someone who caused the harm in the first place.
example: Vaadu thanne naashan, ippol sahaaayikaandaanu — aadine chathichhavan kodukkan vanna marunnu.

literal_meaning: Where ghosts gather, God is not present.
figurative_meaning: Where there is corruption and wrongdoing, goodness cannot thrive.
example: Aa office il sathyam illaaval — bhootham koodiya idatthu daivam illa.

literal_meaning: One task at a time.
figurative_meaning: Focus on one thing at a time for the best results.
example: Randhu kaaranam onnichaayaal rendum maalikkyukayilla — oru neram oru jaoli.

literal_meaning: The one who eats with you will sit with you.
figurative_meaning: People who share resources and meals with you are your true companions.
example: Kashtakaalatthu koode nillu — koode unnarunnavan koode irikkum.

literal_meaning: Do one thing and one thing returns.
figurative_meaning: Every action has an equal and corresponding reaction or outcome.
example: Nee avare help cheythaal avaru ninneyum — onnu cheythaal onnu kittum.

literal_meaning: The past will not return.
figurative_meaning: Time lost cannot be recovered; act in the present.
example: Avashyam ippo cheyyuka — kazhinja kaalam thirichhu varilla.

literal_meaning: A flying bird will land with broken wings.
figurative_meaning: Pride and overconfidence lead to a hard fall.
example: Vaadu etreyum above aayi, ippol thazheyettirrikkunnu — parakkunna kili chirakhodinnjiranngunm.

literal_meaning: Fortune that came without being remembered or expected.
figurative_meaning: Unexpected good luck that arrives without planning.
example: Avan expect cheyyaathe job kitti — orkaathe vanna bhaagyam.

literal_meaning: Thinking and thinking leads to lethargy.
figurative_meaning: Overthinking leads to paralysis and inaction.
example: Plan maathram aandu, aarum start cheyyunilla — aalochicch aalochicch aalasyam.

literal_meaning: Leaves will fall, but the root will remain.
figurative_meaning: Surface-level things change, but core foundations endure.
example: Aarum poyi, kutumbam nilkkum — ilakal kozhinjupokum, veru nilkkum.

literal_meaning: A small boat, a deep sea.
figurative_meaning: A person with limited ability facing a very large challenge.
example: Ivide experience illaathe oru valiya project — cheriya vallam aazhammulla kadal.

literal_meaning: Don't say one thing and do another.
figurative_meaning: Be consistent between your words and your actions.
example: Avanu ippol parayunnathum cheyyunnathum verthey — onnu parayunnu onnu cheyyaruthu.

literal_meaning: Food will be eaten, sleep will be slept.
figurative_meaning: Life's basic rhythms continue regardless of circumstances; things normalize.
example: Ippo ithrem kashtam thonn, pakshe kaalathinnu kaaryam undaakum — bhakshanam bhakshikkum urakam urakkum.

literal_meaning: The one who laughs once will cry once too.
figurative_meaning: Joy and sorrow take turns; no one escapes either.
example: Avanu ippo santosham, pinne kashtam varaam — orikkal chirikkunavan orikkal karayum.

literal_meaning: One God for one person.
figurative_meaning: Everyone has their own source of strength or support; don't depend on others entirely.
example: Swanthaayi nilkkanam — oraalku oru daivam.

idiom: ആനയ്ക്ക് ഒരു ദോഷം, കൊതുകിന് ഒരു ദോഷം
literal_meaning: A flaw for the elephant, a flaw for the mosquito.
figurative_meaning: Everyone, great or small, has their own weakness.
example: Avanum valiyaval, avanum thettu cheyyunnu — anaykku oru dosham, kothukin oru dosham.

literal_meaning: Ask one thing and receive a hundred.
figurative_meaning: A single honest question can yield abundant insight or help.
example: Doubt undenkil chodik — onnu chodichhaal nooru kittum.

literal_meaning: Only as far as the eye can see.
figurative_meaning: People tend to only care about or plan for what is immediately visible to them; short-sightedness.
example: Long term plan illaathe mattram ippo noka — kannu kaanunna idam vare maathram.

literal_meaning: If you don't like it, get out.
figurative_meaning: Take it or leave it; no room for complaints.
example: Avanodu verum oru vaakku — ishtamillengil irangi poo.

literal_meaning: Things don't happen just because you cry.
figurative_meaning: Complaining and lamenting solve nothing; action is needed.
example: Karayaathe pani cheyyoo — karanjaal kittunnathallla kaaryam.

literal_meaning: The time that has gone will not return.
figurative_meaning: The past cannot be recovered; do not waste the present.
example: Poya divasam poya divasam — poya kaalam thirichuvaryilla.

literal_meaning: One who cannot sleep blames the bed.
figurative_meaning: A bad workman blames his tools.
example: Avan pooranaayi fail aayittu question kashtamaayirunnu ennaa parayunnathu — urakkam kettavan kidakka kuttam parayum.

literal_meaning: One group under one roof.
figurative_meaning: Unity and togetherness under a common cause or leadership.
example: Aarum verum thakararathe pani cheythu — oru koorakkuk keezil oru koottam.

literal_meaning: Do not believe everything you hear.
figurative_meaning: Be skeptical; rumors and hearsay are unreliable.
example: Vaarthakal sherikkaanoo enna ariyathe parachathuvinnaa — kettathellam vishwasikkaruthu.

literal_meaning: Good health is the greatest fortune.
figurative_meaning: Health is more valuable than any wealth.
example: Panamaanaalum arogyam poyaal vashamillla — aarogyame mahaa bhaagyam.

literal_meaning: Do not give advice when not asked.
figurative_meaning: Unsolicited advice is unwelcome and disrespectful.
example: Aval chodyichu ennillaatthe nee parayaruthu — chodyikkathe upadeshm kodukkkaruthu.

literal_meaning: They take away the ladder once you've climbed the steps.
figurative_meaning: People remove the means of progress for others once they themselves have benefited.
example: Vaadu career undakkiyathu avare vachu; ippol avare theettunnuu — enipadi ozhinja sesham eni edukum.

literal_meaning: Even one born with you can become an enemy.
figurative_meaning: No relationship guarantees loyalty; even siblings can betray you.
example: Avan shodaran thanne — koode janichhavanum shatruvakum.

literal_meaning: Small boat, small load.
figurative_meaning: Take on only as much as your capacity allows.
example: Ippol ithu mathi, korachu korachu cheyyam — cheriya thoonikku cheriya bhaaram.

literal_meaning: Do what you love, and love will come.
figurative_meaning: Passion leads to mastery and fulfillment.
example: Nee aagraham ullathu therinju padikku — ishtamullath cheythal ishtam varum.

literal_meaning: Trouble if you eat, trouble if you don't.
figurative_meaning: A situation where every option leads to a problem; a no-win situation.
example: Cheytuam kashtam, cheyyaatuam kashtam — tinnaal dosham, tinnaatyirunnal dosham.

literal_meaning: A crooked tree has a crooked shadow.
figurative_meaning: A person's nature is reflected in everything they produce or influence.
example: Avante team kooda avane pole — valanja marattinu valanja nizhal.

literal_meaning: An empty vessel makes noise.
figurative_meaning: People with little substance make the most noise.
example: Vaadu valiya aaL annu parayannu vattunnnu, kazhivu onnum illa — ozhinja paatram occha vekkum.

literal_meaning: The past time is past.
figurative_meaning: Stop dwelling on the past; move forward.
example: Athu muzhuvan kzhiyanjathaanu — kazhinja kaalam kazhiyunju.

literal_meaning: The wise man walks alone.
figurative_meaning: Truly wise people do not need the crowd's validation.
example: Vaadu aarkum poyi parayathe swantham vali theranjedukkunnnu — buddhi ullavan ottakku nadakkum.

literal_meaning: After the rain stops, the sun will come.
figurative_meaning: Hardship is temporary; better times always follow.
example: Ippol kashtamaa, pakshe sheriyvum — mazha thornnal veyil varum.

idiom: ഒരു കൈ നൽകിയാൽ ഒരു കൈ തിരിച്ചു കിട്ടും
literal_meaning: Give one hand, receive one hand in return.
figurative_meaning: What you give to others comes back to you.
example: Avanodu sneham kaattiyathu moolam avanu koottukaaraan kitti — oru kai nalgiyal oru kai thirichhu kittum.

literal_meaning: Studying after three o'clock (too late in the day).
figurative_meaning: Starting to prepare when it is already too late.
example: Exam naalye, ippol padikkaanirikkunnnu — moonnu mani kazhinyathu padikkunnathu.

literal_meaning: A sharp-minded person will not fall into a pit.
figurative_meaning: Intelligence and foresight keep you out of trouble.
example: Vaadu mundey thanne itharinju — koorma buddhi ullavan kuzhiyil veezilla.

literal_meaning: One must manage with what one has.
figurative_meaning: Be content and resourceful with what is available.
example: Ippol ithu mathi ennu manassilaakkoo — ullatu kondu otungikkazhiyaanam.

literal_meaning: No one remembers anyone.
figurative_meaning: People are forgotten quickly once they are gone or no longer useful.
example: Vaadu poyi, aarum thirichhunokkiyilla — aarum aare orkkyilla.

literal_meaning: A fallen leaf cannot rejoin the branch.
figurative_meaning: Some separations and losses are permanent and irreversible.
example: Aa bandham thutinju — kozhinja ila thirichhu cheriyilla.

literal_meaning: What God gives cannot be stopped by anyone.
figurative_meaning: Destiny and fortune cannot be blocked by human intervention.
example: Avanu kitten ennundu ennal kittoum — daivam kodukkunnath aarkkum tadayaan kaziyilla.

literal_meaning: Do not blame the light while sitting in the darkness.
figurative_meaning: Do not criticize what you yourself are refusing or failing to embrace.
example: Avan padikkaathe padippinopp kuttam parayunnu — iruttath irnnu velichath kuttam parayaaruthu.

literal_meaning: Until drawing one's last wheezed breath.
figurative_meaning: Until the very end of life; to the last moment.
example: Vaadu porunnathu vare pani cheyth — chakrasvaasam valikkunnathuvare.

literal_meaning: A borrowed elephant seems to have bigger tusks.
figurative_meaning: People show off borrowed or temporary things as if they were their own.
example: Vaadu avaante car vaangichi parade nadattunnu — kadam vaangiya aanakku kombu kooduthal.

literal_meaning: The one who works will gain employment.
figurative_meaning: Hard work and initiative create their own opportunities.
example: Vaadu kaaththirikkunnilla swayam sheramikkunnu — jooli cheyyunnavan thozhil nedum.

idiom: ഒരു ദിക്കിൽ ഉദിക്കും, മറ്റൊരു ദിക്കിൽ അസ്തമിക്കും
literal_meaning: Rises in one direction, sets in another.
figurative_meaning: A person's influence or fortune shifts over time and context.
example: Avan oru kalathu valiyavanaayrunu, ippol arum vekkunnilla — oru dikkil udikkum, mattoru dikkil asthamikkkum.

literal_meaning: The ghost that has gone is gone.
figurative_meaning: What is over is over; no point revisiting the past.
example: Aa vishayam kazhinju — bhootham poya bhootham.

idiom: മൂർഖൻ ഒരു ദോഷം ചെയ്‌താൽ നൂറ് ദോഷം ഉണ്ടാകും
literal_meaning: If a fool commits one wrong, a hundred wrongs follow.
figurative_meaning: A foolish action creates cascading problems.
example: Avan oru tappu cheythu, ippol annekaare aayi — moorkkhan oru dosham cheythal nooru dosham undakum.

literal_meaning: First think, then act.
figurative_meaning: Careful thought before action prevents regret.
example: Oru randu minutu irikku, pinne cheyyoo — aadyam chinthikkuka, pinne pravartthikkuka.

literal_meaning: If there is prosperity in the home, the head of the house prospers.
figurative_meaning: The wellbeing of the household reflects the wellbeing of its leader.
example: Varum varavin koottuttil sherivaakumbol varum — gruhatthil aishwaryam undenghil gruhanathan aishwaryavaan.

literal_meaning: A rolling stone does not settle in one place.
figurative_meaning: A restless person who keeps moving never builds stability.
example: Vaadu oru sthalathu nilkkaatthe nadakkunnu — urulunna kallu oru idatthu urakkilla.

literal_meaning: What is not inside cannot be seen outside.
figurative_meaning: A person can only show outwardly what they truly possess within.
example: Sneham illaattevan sneham nadinikkukayillla — ullil illaathathu veliyil kaanilla.

literal_meaning: The one who loses must run twice as fast.
figurative_meaning: After a failure, you must work twice as hard to recover.
example: Oru thaval pazhichu, ippol ore aagraha thode tirichu vaa — thottavan iratti odanam.

literal_meaning: Let what is far away remain far away.
figurative_meaning: Do not meddle in matters that do not concern you.
example: Avante vishayam avarkku vittukoo — doorey ullath doorey irikkatte.

literal_meaning: A smiling face, an unsmiling heart.
figurative_meaning: Outward cheerfulness concealing inner pain or deceit.
example: Vaadu enninaum chirikunnu, pakshe ullil kashtam — chirikkunna mukham chirikkaatha manass.

literal_meaning: A knowledgeable person does not judge.
figurative_meaning: True wisdom brings humility and understanding, not judgment.
example: Avanu ariyaam, pakshe onninum parayaaru — jnaanam ullavan jajj cheyyilla.

literal_meaning: A tree without roots will fall.
figurative_meaning: Anything without a strong foundation will eventually collapse.
example: Company culture sheri alla, ennaal thurannu poyi — verillaatha maram veezum.

literal_meaning: One word can win a thousand battles.
figurative_meaning: The right words spoken at the right time can be more powerful than force.
example: Avante oru vaaakku situation thirichu — oru vaakk ayiram yuddham jayikkum.

literal_meaning: When the eclipse passes, the light returns.
figurative_meaning: Difficult times are temporary; clarity and goodness will return.
example: Ee kashtam maarttipookum — grahanam maariyaal velicham varum.

literal_meaning: The responsibility you have taken must be carried through.
figurative_meaning: Once you accept a duty, you must fulfill it completely.
example: Vaakku koduththathu thirikkanam — yettta uttaravaadithvam yettu nadakkkanam.

idiom: ഓടാത്ത കാൽ ഓടും ഓടിയ കാൽ ക്ഷീണിക്കും
literal_meaning: The leg that did not run will run; the leg that ran will tire.
figurative_meaning: Everyone has their moment; those who rush tire, those who wait get their turn.
example: Aa samayam varum, kaathirikkoo — odaatha kaal odum, odiya kaal ksheenikkum.

literal_meaning: Play with what is in your hand.
figurative_meaning: Make the best use of the resources you currently have.
example: Ippol ithey ullu, ithukond chesyyam — kayyil ullath kondu kalikkoo.

literal_meaning: No need to walk back the same path you walked.
figurative_meaning: Do not repeat past mistakes or return to what you have moved on from.
example: Aa sambhavam marannu munde poo — nadannavazhi thinne thirichchu nadakkkand.

literal_meaning: Do not search awake for what you saw in a dream.
figurative_meaning: Do not chase fantasies or illusions as if they were real.
example: Avan yathaarthyam illaatha plan tharanu pinthudarnnu — urakkatthil kandathine unarnnu thedaruthu.

literal_meaning: You can make a torch from a dry leaf.
figurative_meaning: Even something small or insignificant can be made useful.
example: Chinna budget aayirunnu, pakshe nallorunnu cheythu — kariyila kondu kolli undaakkam.

idiom: ഒരു ദിവസം ഒരു നൂൽ നൂൽക്കുന്നവൻ ഒരു വർഷം ഒരു വസ്ത്രം ഉണ്ടാക്കും
literal_meaning: One who spins one thread a day will make one garment in a year.
figurative_meaning: Consistent small efforts accumulate into a great result.
example: Rozhum oru page ezhuthiyaal novel theerum — oru divasam oru nool noolkkunavan.

literal_meaning: From the crown of the head to the sole of the foot.
figurative_meaning: Completely; through and through; from top to bottom.
example: Aa vishayam uchi muthal ullam kaal vare ariyam.

literal_meaning: One who has eyes will see.
figurative_meaning: The truth is visible to anyone willing to look.
example: Avarum undaakirunnu, enkilum kaanaathe nadinchhu — kannu ullaavan kaanum.

literal_meaning: A snake will bite one already struck by lightning.
figurative_meaning: Troubles pile on those who are already suffering.
example: Naukri poyitti, ippol arogya prasnayum — idivettiyavane pambu kadikkum.

literal_meaning: A friendship that cuts the throat.
figurative_meaning: A relationship that appears friendly but is actually harmful.
example: Vaadu ente rahasym vellatthi — kazhuthu murrikkunna sauhrudam.

literal_meaning: It does not truly belong to anyone.
figurative_meaning: Shared or public things are often neglected by everyone.
example: Office pantry aarkkum swantham allathathukond villakkam illaathayi — aarkkum aarkkum ullathalla.

literal_meaning: One who spends life criticizing.
figurative_meaning: A chronic fault-finder who never contributes anything positive.
example: Vaadu always others ne criticize cheyyunnu, swayam onnum cheyyunilla — kuttam paryunnu kazhinunavan.

literal_meaning: One must face the current.
figurative_meaning: You must confront challenges head-on rather than avoid them.
example: Kashtam vannapol ozhivaarkaruthu — ozhukine nerridaanam.

literal_meaning: A city was not built in a single day.
figurative_meaning: Great things take time and sustained effort.
example: Ippolthanne result venam ennu chinthikkanda — ororttaa divasam kondu nagaram panitthilla.

literal_meaning: Do not change the wheel of a moving vehicle.
figurative_meaning: Do not make major changes to something that is already working.
example: System nannaayi pani cheyyunnu, ippol maattanda — odunna vandikku chakram maattarruthu.

literal_meaning: A single blow will not dislodge a stone.
figurative_meaning: Persistent effort is needed; one attempt is rarely enough.
example: First try il result kitttiyilla, thudarnnu cheyyanam — otta adikku oru kallu ilakilla.

literal_meaning: Hope only after seeing the person.
figurative_meaning: Do not count on help until it is actually in front of you.
example: Vaadu varum ennuth nishchayam illla — aale kanditu aasha.

literal_meaning: Do not forget at night what you did during the day.
figurative_meaning: Be consistent in your actions; do not contradict yourself.
example: Avan pakal parayunnathu, raatri thallipparayyunnu — pakal cheytathu raatri marakkkaruthu.

literal_meaning: A relationship drawing its last breath.
figurative_meaning: A relationship or partnership that is on the verge of complete breakdown.
example: Avarum thammil maathadam onnumill — oorddhvaswaasam vallikkunna bandham.

literal_meaning: A broken ship will not float.
figurative_meaning: A fundamentally flawed system or plan cannot succeed.
example: Athi kashtamaayi design chessu, ippol fail — polinjna kappal ozhukilla.

idiom: തോർക്കാൻ ഒരു കൈ, കൂട്ടാൻ ഒരു കൈ
literal_meaning: One hand to wipe, one hand to gather.
figurative_meaning: Every loss must be balanced by a gain; life has give and take.
example: Oru pani poyirunnu, matoru kittu — thorkkaan oru kai, koottaan oru kai.

literal_meaning: Where there is health, there is joy.
figurative_meaning: Good health is the foundation of happiness.
example: Panam undu, pakshe arogym illa — aarogym ullideltthu aanandam.

literal_meaning: Unwanted advice is poison.
figurative_meaning: Advice given without being asked can do more harm than good.
example: Avan chodyikkathe cheppan poyi, avalu vexed aayi — vendaatha updesham visham.

literal_meaning: Strike the iron while it is hot.
figurative_meaning: Act at the right moment when conditions are favourable.
example: Offer vachinappazhe accept cheyyaayirunnu — chooduullapol irimbu adikkanam.

literal_meaning: One country, one language.
figurative_meaning: Unity of purpose and communication creates a cohesive community.
example: Team oru dikhile pokanam — oru desham oru bhaasha.

literal_meaning: Do not go to the market to gather mud.
figurative_meaning: Do not engage in or bring home troubles from outside.
example: Offisu kakkaattu vaarthakal veettil parayanda — chanthayil chennu chali vaaranda.

literal_meaning: Do not break the pot by weeping over it.
figurative_meaning: Do not let grief or frustration cause you to destroy what you have.
example: Panicchu theruvu mutthi kudikkanda — karannju kalam udaykkaruthu.

literal_meaning: Remember your loved ones and give what you have.
figurative_meaning: Cherish and be generous with those close to you.
example: Avarum doorey aayanappol manassilaayii — uttavare orkkkanam, ullath kodukkkanam.

literal_meaning: There is sound, but no strength.
figurative_meaning: All talk and no capability; noise without substance.
example: Vaadu meetings il valiya vaakkukal parayum, cheyyum onnum — shabdam undu, shakti illa.

literal_meaning: What God created, God will destroy.
figurative_meaning: Everything that exists will eventually end; impermanence is universal.
example: Athum itum ellam kaalam theerumbo teerrum — daivam srushtichathum daivam nashipikkum.

literal_meaning: Strength fit for an elephant.
figurative_meaning: Extraordinary power or capacity, suited only to the strongest.
example: Avanu aarum cheyya kazhiyaatha pani cheythu — anaykku aanakkarutth.

literal_meaning: Silence is consent.
figurative_meaning: Not speaking up is taken as agreement.
example: Vaadu onnum parayanilla, athinu artham shari ennaa — mounam sammtham.

literal_meaning: One who is with you must walk alongside.
figurative_meaning: A true partner must keep pace and not fall behind or race ahead.
example: Team member avarude pace il pani cheyyaarunilla — koode ullavan oppam nadakkanam.

literal_meaning: A wolf in sheep's clothing.
figurative_meaning: Someone who pretends to be harmless or good but is actually dangerous.
example: Vaadu nalla polirikkum, pakshe ullil vera — aattin tholida chennaayi.

literal_meaning: When a pot is full, it overflows.
figurative_meaning: Every person has a limit to their patience; push too far and they will react.
example: Avan ithuvare sahinchhu, ippol pottity — oru kudam nirannjal kaviyum.

literal_meaning: Like looking at the palm of your hand.
figurative_meaning: Something is perfectly clear and obvious.
example: Sathyam ullam kai nokkunnapole spashttam — enthu proof venam.

literal_meaning: An umbrella that won't bow under one roof.
figurative_meaning: A person who refuses to submit to any authority.
example: Vaadu aareyum kuttaakkarunilla — oru koorakku keezh padaatha chatram.

literal_meaning: The earth does not fear lightning.
figurative_meaning: A grounded and stable person is not shaken by sudden threats or outbursts.
example: Avante oru vaakku kond avan tharimaarunilla — idiminnaal bhoomi bhayakkilla.

literal_meaning: A flame untouched by wind.
figurative_meaning: Someone who is not influenced by outside pressure or opinion.
example: Avante focus maaraattha — kaattu elkaatha deepam.

literal_meaning: One small and one big.
figurative_meaning: A mismatched pair; two things that do not belong together.
example: Aavarude team balance illaatha — onnu cheruthum onnu valu.

literal_meaning: Remember before you die.
figurative_meaning: Do not put off what is important; act while you still have time.
example: Avide poi nokkanam, ippol kazhiyuvolam — marikkunnathin munpu orkkkanam.

literal_meaning: First prepare, then step out.
figurative_meaning: Always prepare thoroughly before starting anything.
example: Interview ki pokathe munpe research cheyyaayirunnu — aadyam orungoo, pinne irangoo.

literal_meaning: A place where the household goddess resides.
figurative_meaning: A home that is blessed with warmth, prosperity, and harmony.
example: Avar veettil oru special atmosphere undu — gruhalakshmi ulla idam.

literal_meaning: An empty place, an empty mind.
figurative_meaning: Idleness leads to negative or wandering thoughts.
example: Vaadu oru pani cheyyunilla, maanasika prasnangal koodi — ozhinja sthalatthu ozhinja manass.

literal_meaning: A lamp that once burned will burn again.
figurative_meaning: Someone who was once great can rise again.
example: Vaadu oru kaalathu nannaayi undaayrunu, ippol tirichu vannu — orikkal kattthiya vilakku veendum katttum.

literal_meaning: Eat the food you have and live.
figurative_meaning: Be content with what you have instead of craving more.
example: Expectations kurakkoo — ulla oonu undu jeevikkoo.

literal_meaning: One glance is equal to a thousand words.
figurative_meaning: A look can communicate what no amount of words can.
example: Avanu ennodu oru nokkam mathi, artham ayi — oru nottam ayiram vaakinu tulyam.

literal_meaning: Where there is running, there is also falling.
figurative_meaning: Ambition and action carry the risk of failure.
example: Risk edukkathe avanghottilla — odunnidaltthu veechayum undu.

literal_meaning: The one who brought it must give it.
figurative_meaning: Whoever created the problem is responsible for fixing it.
example: Vaade aa situation undaakki, vaade resolve cheyyaanam — konduvannavan kodukkkanam.

literal_meaning: The leaf and the thorn sit together.
figurative_meaning: Good and bad always coexist; you cannot have one without the other.
example: Ivide nallathum kettathum ondicchirikkum — ilayum mullum orumich irikkum.

idiom: ഒരു ദോഷം മറക്കൂ, ഒരു ഗുണം ഓർക്കൂ
literal_meaning: Forget one fault, remember one virtue.
figurative_meaning: Focus on the good in others rather than their flaws.
example: Avante oru tappu kaanaathe nadinchu — oru dosham marakku, oru gunam orkku.

literal_meaning: Crying is useless; live by smiling.
figurative_meaning: Adopt a positive attitude; wallowing in sorrow changes nothing.
example: Kaaryam kazhinjtu, ippol munde pookoo — karanjhu phalamill, chirichu jeevikkoo.

literal_meaning: A mistake can be forgiven once.
figurative_meaning: Forgiveness is possible for a first mistake, but repeated offenses cannot be excused.
example: Avar oru thaval kshamichchu, randaam thaval aavilla — thettu orikkal kshamikkam.

literal_meaning: One smile can remove a thousand sorrows.
figurative_meaning: Positivity and warmth have great healing power.
example: Avante oru chiri avarude sadanam maattti — oru chiri aaayiram dukham maattum.

literal_meaning: To see and hear.
figurative_meaning: To be aware of something.
example: He is well-informed about the situation; he can see and hear everything.

literal_meaning: If a bird flies in the sky.
figurative_meaning: Something that is unlikely to happen.
example: If he wins the lottery, it will be like a bird flying in the sky.

literal_meaning: If it gets into the eye.
figurative_meaning: Something that is very close or personal.
example: This issue is very close to my heart; it's like it gets into my eye.

literal_meaning: To break the egg.
figurative_meaning: To take a bold step or risk.
example: He decided to break the egg and start his own business.

literal_meaning: To shed tears.
figurative_meaning: To express deep sorrow or emotion.
example: She couldn't help but shed tears during the emotional movie.

literal_meaning: To get into water.
figurative_meaning: To face difficulties or challenges.
example: He got into water while trying to complete the project on time.

literal_meaning: The fragrance of a flower.
figurative_meaning: Something beautiful or pleasant.
example: Her smile is like the fragrance of a flower, bringing joy to everyone.

literal_meaning: To bathe in the eye.
figurative_meaning: To be very close or dear.
example: That memory is so precious; it feels like I bathed in the eye.

literal_meaning: To flow in the river.
figurative_meaning: To go with the flow or adapt.
example: In life, sometimes you just have to flow in the river and see where it takes you.

literal_meaning: The jasmine in the front yard has no fragrance.
figurative_meaning: Familiarity breeds contempt; undervaluing what is easily available.
example: Avan swantham nattile kalakaranmare bahumanikkilla, muttathe mullakku manamillallo.

idiom: പല തുള്ളി പെരുവെള്ളം (Pala thulli peru vellam)
literal_meaning: Many drops make a great flood.
figurative_meaning: Little contributions add up to a massive result.
example: Kooduthal aalkar sahayichal ee project theerkam, pala thulli peru vellam aanallo.

literal_meaning: All that glitters is not gold.
figurative_meaning: Appearances can be deceptive.
example: Aa puthiya investment thട്ടിppaayirunnu, minnunnathellam ponnalla ennu ippol manassilayi.

idiom: കാക്കയ്ക്കും തൻ കുഞ്ഞ് പൊൻകുഞ്ഞ് (Kakkakkum than kunju pon kunju)
literal_meaning: Even to a crow, its own child is a golden child.
figurative_meaning: Everyone loves their own offspring dearly, regardless of flaws.
example: Avan ethra thettu cheythalum ammakku avan nallavana, kakkakkum than kunju pon kunjanallo.

idiom: എരിയുന്ന തീയിൽ എണ്ണ ഒഴിക്കുക (Eriyunna theeyil enna ozhikkuka)
literal_meaning: To pour oil into a burning fire.
figurative_meaning: To make a bad situation worse; adding fuel to the fire.
example: Avar thammil ulla prashnathil nee idapedanda, eriyunna theeyil enna ozhikkunnu.

literal_meaning: Does a donkey know the smell of camphor?
figurative_meaning: An uncultured person cannot appreciate the value of fine things.
example: Ee nalla sangeetham avan manassilavilla, kazhuthaykkariyamo karpoorathinte manam.

idiom: മിണ്ടാപ്പൂച്ച കലം ഉ‌ടയ്ക്കും (Minda poocha kalam udaikkum)
literal_meaning: The silent cat breaks the pot.
figurative_meaning: Quiet people can sometimes be the most mischievous or surprising.
example: Avan onnum mindillengilum achanodu ellam paranju, minda poocha kalam udaikkum.

literal_meaning: Only a snake knows a snake's legs.
figurative_meaning: It takes one to know one; people of similar nature understand each other.
example: Kallante budhi kallane ariyu, paambinte kaalu paambariyum.

idiom: വേലിയിൽ ഇരുന്ന പാമ്പിനെ എടുത്തു തോളിൽ വയ്ക്കുക (Veliyil irunna paambine eduthu tholil vaykuka)
literal_meaning: Taking a snake sitting on the fence and putting it on the shoulder.
figurative_meaning: To unnecessarily invite trouble into one's life.
example: Veruthe avante prashnathil idapettu, veliyil irunna paambine tholil vechathu poleyayi.

idiom: ചക്ക വീണത് മുയൽ ചത്തത് (Chakka veenathu muyal chathathu)
literal_meaning: The jackfruit fell, the rabbit died.
figurative_meaning: A pure coincidence mistaken for cause and effect.
example: Avan officeil ninnu poyathum current vannu, chakka veenathu muyal chathathu pole.

idiom: വേലി തന്നെ വിളവു തിന്നുക (Veli thanne vilavu thinnuka)
literal_meaning: The fence itself eating the crop.
figurative_meaning: The protector turning into the predator.
example: Police kaaran thanne moshanam nadathiyal pinne enth cheyyan? Veli thanne vilavu thinnukayanu.

literal_meaning: Will a crow become a crane if it bathes?
figurative_meaning: You cannot change someone's inherent nature with superficial changes.
example: Avan ethra panam undakkiyalum avante swabhavam maarilla, kaakka kulichal kokkakumo?

idiom: വൈദ്യൻ കല്പിച്ചതും രോഗി ഇച്ഛിച്ചതും പാല് (Vaidyan kalpichathum rogi ichichathum paalu)
literal_meaning: What the doctor prescribed and what the patient desired was milk.
figurative_meaning: A win-win situation where advice perfectly matches desires.
example: Enikku pokan madi aayirunnu, appozha event maattivechathu, vaidyan kalpichathum rogi ichichathum paalu.

literal_meaning: Celebrate like Onam with whatever is available.
figurative_meaning: Make the best out of what you have.
example: Ee cheriya veettil namukku santhoshikkanam, ullathukondu onam pole.

idiom: അക്കരെ നിന്നാൽ ഇക്കരെ പച്ച (Akkare ninnal ikkare paccha)
literal_meaning: From the other shore, this shore looks green.
figurative_meaning: The grass is always greener on the other side.
example: Avanu vadeshathe jeevitham valiya ishtamanu, pakshe akkare ninnal ikkare paccha aanu.

idiom: ആന മെലിഞ്ഞാൽ തൊഴുത്തിൽ കെട്ടാമോ (Aana melinjal thozhuthil kettamo)
literal_meaning: If an elephant becomes thin, can it be tied in a cowshed?
figurative_meaning: Even in decline, a great person or thing retains their inherent stature.
example: Avarude kudumbam ippol daridryathilanengilum avarude anthassu poyitilla, aana melinjal thozhuthil kettamo.

idiom: പടപേടിച്ച് പന്തളത്ത് ചെന്നപ്പോൾ അവിടെ പന്തം കൊളുത്തി പട (Pada pedichu panthalathu chennappol avide pantham koluthi pada)
literal_meaning: Feared the war and went to Panthalam, only to find a war with torches there.
figurative_meaning: Out of the frying pan and into the fire.
example: Nattile prashnam pedichu townil vannappol ivide athilum valiya prashnam, pada pedichu panthalathu chennappol poleyayi.

literal_meaning: What does a coconut mean to a dog?
figurative_meaning: Giving something valuable to someone who cannot appreciate or use it.
example: Avanu ee puthiya laptop koduthathu verutheyayi, naaykkenthu thenga.

idiom: താൻ പിടിച്ച മുയലിന് കൊമ്പ് മൂന്ന് (Thaan pidicha muyalinu kombu moonnu)
literal_meaning: The rabbit I caught has three horns.
figurative_meaning: Stubbornly clinging to a false or absurd claim.
example: Avan parayunnathu thettanennu thelinjittum sammathikkilla, thaan pidicha muyalinu kombu moonnu enna avastha.

idiom: ചുട്ടയിലെ ശീലം ചുടല വരെ (Chuttayile sheelam chudala vare)
literal_meaning: Habits formed in the cradle last till the funeral pyre.
figurative_meaning: Old habits die hard.
example: Avan eppozhum kalla parayum, athu maarilla, chuttayile sheelam chudala vare.

idiom: എലിയെ പേടിച്ച് ഇല്ലം ചുടുക (Eliye pedichu illam chuduka)
literal_meaning: Burning the house out of fear of a rat.
figurative_meaning: Taking an extreme or destructive measure to solve a small problem.
example: Cheruthaaya problem solve cheyyan company thanne adaikkunnathu eliye pedichu illam chudunnathu poleyanu.

idiom: ഓടുന്ന നായയ്ക്ക് ഒരു മുഴം മുമ്പേ (Odunna naayakku oru muzham mumpe)
literal_meaning: Throwing the stick a yard ahead of the running dog.
figurative_meaning: Being highly proactive; anticipating actions before they happen.
example: Market maarunnathinu munpe avar product maatti, odunna naayakku oru muzham mumpe.

idiom: കരിമ്പു കാട്ടിൽ ആന കയറിയതു പോലെ (Karimbu kattil aana kayariyathu pole)
literal_meaning: Like an elephant entering a sugarcane field.
figurative_meaning: Being in a state of absolute joy with unlimited access to what one loves.
example: Sweets shopil kayariya kuttiye kandal karimbu kattil aana kayariyathu poleyanu.

idiom: പട്ടി കുരച്ചാൽ പല്ലക്ക് നിൽക്കുമോ (Patti kurachal pallakku nilkkumo)
literal_meaning: Will the palanquin stop if a dog barks?
figurative_meaning: The progress of the great will not be stopped by the criticism of the insignificant.
example: Avarude parihasangal kettu nee pinmaranda, patti kurachal pallakku nilkkumo.

literal_meaning: The fox's eyes are always on the chicken coop.
figurative_meaning: A person with ulterior motives always focuses on their target.
example: Avan nallathu parayunnundengilum kurukkante kannu kozhikkoottil aanu.

literal_meaning: The tail shouldn't wag when the head is present.
figurative_meaning: Subordinates should not overstep when the leader is present.
example: MD ivide ullappol nee theerumanam edukkaruthu, thalayirikkumbol vaaladaruthu.

idiom: പാല് കുടിച്ച പാമ്പും കടിക്കും (Paalu kudicha paambum kadikkum)
literal_meaning: Even a snake fed with milk will bite.
figurative_meaning: A wicked person will betray you even if you treat them well.
example: Avanodu nannayi perumariyittum chathichu, paalu kudicha paambum kadikkum.

idiom: മീൻ കുഞ്ഞിനെ നീന്താൻ പഠിപ്പിക്കണോ (Meen kunjine neenthan padippikkano)
literal_meaning: Do you need to teach a baby fish how to swim?
figurative_meaning: You don't need to teach someone what they are naturally talented at.
example: Avanu coding ariyamo ennu chodhikkanda, meen kunjine neenthan padippikkano.

literal_meaning: If there is unity, you can sleep even on a pestle.
figurative_meaning: Any difficult situation is manageable if people stand united.
example: Ee prathisandhiyil namukku orumichu nilkkam, orumayundengil ulakkamelum kidakkam.

idiom: മുങ്ങിച്ചാവാൻ പോകുന്നവൻ കച്ചിത്തുരുമ്പും പിടിക്കും (Mungichavan pokunnavan kachithurumbum pidikkum)
literal_meaning: A drowning man will catch even a straw.
figurative_meaning: A desperate person will try any small chance to save themselves.
example: Avan last chanceum upayogichu, mungichavan pokunnavan kachithurumbum pidikkum.

literal_meaning: Will a crow fly upside down?
figurative_meaning: Something that is completely impossible.
example: Avan enne sahayikkum ennu ne karuthunnuvo, kaakka malarnnu parakkumo?

idiom: ഉപ്പു തിന്നവൻ വെള്ളം കുടിക്കും (Uppu thinnavan vellam kudikkum)
literal_meaning: He who eats salt will drink water.
figurative_meaning: You will have to face the consequences of your wrong actions.
example: Thettu cheythathu pidikkappettu, uppu thinnavan vellam kudikkum.

literal_meaning: Even a squirrel does what it can.
figurative_meaning: Every small contribution matters.
example: Enikondu aavunna sahayam njan cheythu, annarakkannanum thannalayathu.

literal_meaning: Like a tree with its roots cut.
figurative_meaning: Completely helpless and falling.
example: Swaytham business pottiyappol avan verarutha maram pole aayi.

literal_meaning: Remove a thorn using another thorn.
figurative_meaning: Fight fire with fire; use a bad thing to cure another bad thing.
example: Avanude kallatharam kandupidikkan mullu kondu mulledukkanam.

literal_meaning: Winnow when the wind blows.
figurative_meaning: Make hay while the sun shines; seize the opportunity.
example: Avasaram ullappol thanne muthalakkuka, kattullappol pattanam.

literal_meaning: The master can even do it in the stove.
figurative_meaning: Experts or masters are granted exceptions to the rules.
example: Avar rules thettichalum aarum onnum parayilla, aashaanu aduppilum aavam.

idiom: തിളച്ച വെള്ളത്തിൽ വീണ പൂച്ച പച്ചവെള്ളം കണ്ടാലും പേടിക്കും (Thilacha vellathil veena poocha pachavellam kandalum pedikkum)
literal_meaning: A cat that fell in boiling water will fear even cold water.
figurative_meaning: Once bitten, twice shy.
example: Pazhaya experience kaaranam avan onninum thuniyunnilla, thilacha vellathil veena poocha pole.

literal_meaning: Digging where it is wet.
figurative_meaning: Taking the easy way out; exploiting a vulnerable person.
example: Avan ellavarudeyum weakness muthaledukkum, nananjedam kuzhikkuka aanu pathivu.

literal_meaning: What business does a cat have where gold is melted?
figurative_meaning: What business does an ignorant/irrelevant person have in serious matters?
example: Valiyavarude meeingil nee enthina varunne, ponnurukkunnidathu poochakkenthu karyam.

literal_meaning: He who lives by the sword dies by the sword.
figurative_meaning: Those who commit violence will eventually suffer from it.
example: Don aayirunnavan adhe vazhiyil marihcu, valedukkunnavan valal.

idiom: ശ്വാനന്റെ വാല് പന്തീരാണ്ട് കുഴലിലിട്ടാലും വളഞ്ഞു തന്നെ (Shwanante vaalu pantheerandu kuzhalilittalum valanju thanne)
literal_meaning: A dog's tail put in a pipe for 12 years remains crooked.
figurative_meaning: You cannot change the fundamental bad nature of a person.
example: Avanu ethra upadesham koduthalum maarilla, shwanante vaalu kuzhalilittathu pole.

literal_meaning: Chankaran is the perfect match for Chakki.
figurative_meaning: Made for each other, usually used for two similarly flawed people.
example: Avar randum kudi orumichu thettukal cheyyunnu, chakkikkotha chankaran.

idiom: ഇരുന്നിട്ടു വേണം കാലു നീട്ടാൻ (Irunnittu venam kaalu neettan)
literal_meaning: Sit first before stretching your legs.
figurative_meaning: Secure your position before demanding more or acting arrogant.
example: Job sthiramavunnathinu munpe avarodu demand cheyyaruthu, irunnittu venam kaalu neettan.

literal_meaning: What is a bathing step to a water hen?
figurative_meaning: A person who is always wandering has no fixed home or boundaries.
example: Nirantharam yathra cheyyunna avanu sthiramayi oridathu nilkkan aavilla, kulakkozhikku enthu kulikkadavu.

literal_meaning: An attempt to beautify resulted in vitiligo.
figurative_meaning: An attempt to improve a situation made it disastrously worse.
example: System nannakkan sramichathu aake crash aayi, velukkan thechathu paandaayi.

idiom: അൽപ്പന് അർത്ഥം കിട്ടിയാൽ അർദ്ധരാത്രിക്ക് കുട പിടിക്കും (Alpanu artham kittiyal ardharathrikku kuda pidikkum)
literal_meaning: If a mean person gets wealth, he will hold an umbrella at midnight.
figurative_meaning: When an undeserving person gets sudden wealth, they show off foolishly.
example: Lottery adichappol avante ahankaram kandille, alpanu artham kittiyal ardharathrikku kuda pidikkum.

idiom: ഉറുമ്പിനും തന്റെ ജീവൻ വലുതാണ് (Urumbinum thante jeevan valuthaanu)
literal_meaning: Even an ant values its life.
figurative_meaning: Every living being values its own existence, no matter how small.
example: Aareyum drohikkaruthu, urumbinum thante jeevan valuthaanu.

idiom: ചുട്ടു തിന്നാലും വാസന പോവില്ല (Chuttu thinnalum vaasana povilla)
literal_meaning: Even if roasted, the smell won't go.
figurative_meaning: Deep-rooted bad habits cannot be eradicated easily.
example: Avanude kalla swabhavam maarilla, chuttu thinnalum vaasana povilla.

idiom: പുര കത്തുമ്പോൾ വാഴ വെട്ടുക (Pura kathumbol vazha vettuka)
literal_meaning: Cutting the banana tree while the house is burning.
figurative_meaning: Selfishly taking advantage of someone else's disaster.
example: Nattil prashnam nadakkumbol avar swantham karyam nokkunnu, pura kathumbol vazha vettukayanu.

idiom: അടി തെറ്റിയാൽ ആനയും വീഴും (Adi thettiyaal aaneyum veezhum)
literal_meaning: Even an elephant will fall if it takes a wrong step.
figurative_meaning: Even the strongest or most experienced person can fail if they are careless.
example: Avan ethra valiya expert aayalum sradhikkanam, adi thettiyal aaneyum veezhum.

idiom: അക്കരെ നിൽക്കുമ്പോൾ ഇക്കരെ പച്ച (Akkare nilkkumpol ikkare pacha)
literal_meaning: Things look green on this shore from the other shore.
figurative_meaning: The grass is always greener on the other side.
example: Avanu purathu pokan ishtamanu, pakshe akkare nilkkumpol ikkare pacha aanu.

idiom: അനുഭവം ആണ് മഹാ ഗുരു (Anubhavam aanu mahaa guru)
literal_meaning: Experience is the great teacher.
figurative_meaning: You learn the best lessons from your own experiences.
example: Thettukalil ninnu padikku, anubhavam aanu mahaa guru.

literal_meaning: Experience is the seventh sense.
figurative_meaning: True wisdom comes from personal experience.
example: Avarude life lessons kandu padikkanam, ezham arivu anubhavamaanu.

idiom: കണ്ണുള്ളപ്പോൾ കണ്ണിന്റെ വില അറിയില്ല (Kannullappol kanninte vila ariyilla)
literal_meaning: One does not realize the value of eyes while having them.
figurative_meaning: People don't appreciate what they have until they lose it.
example: Achan ulla kalam aarum anweshichilla, kannullappol kanninte vila ariyilla.

idiom: പുഴു തിന്നാത്ത പഴം ഇല്ല (Puzhu thinnatha pazham illa)
literal_meaning: There is no fruit that hasn't been eaten by a worm.
figurative_meaning: No one is completely flawless or perfect.
example: Aarum poornaralla, puzhu thinnatha pazham illa.

literal_meaning: The stone that grinds will produce powder.
figurative_meaning: Consistent hard work will eventually yield results.
example: Nee thudarndu sramikku, araykkunna kall podikkum.

idiom: അട്ടയെപ്പിടിച്ച് മെത്തയിൽ കിടത്തിയാൽ കിടക്കുമോ (Attayepidichu methayil kidathiyaal kidakkumo)
literal_meaning: If you put a leech on a mattress, will it stay there?
figurative_meaning: People naturally revert to their own base environments or habits.
example: Avanu panam kittiyittum pazhaya swabhavam mattiyailla, attayepidichu methayil kidathiyaal kidakkumo?

literal_meaning: A small fruit in an elephant's mouth.
figurative_meaning: An amount that is absurdly too small for a huge need.
example: Ee kuranju shabalam kondu kudumbam pottan aavilla, aana vayil ampazhanga poleyanu.

literal_meaning: A barking dog will not bite.
figurative_meaning: People who make a lot of noise or threats rarely take action.
example: Avan veruthe vaakkukal parayukayanu, kuraykkunna patti kadikkilla.

idiom: കനകം മൂലം കാമിനി മൂലം (Kanakam moolam kaamini moolam)
literal_meaning: Through gold and through a woman.
figurative_meaning: Wealth and women are the root causes of all conflicts in the world.
example: Orupadu war nadannathu kanakam moolam kaamini moolam aanu.

literal_meaning: Do not kill a person without knowing them.
figurative_meaning: Do not judge or punish someone before knowing the full truth about them.
example: Avanude bhagam kelkkuka, aalariyathe aale kollaruthu.

literal_meaning: He who doesn't learn by seeing, learns by getting hit.
figurative_meaning: Some people only learn their lesson the hard way, through painful experience.
example: Avan paranju kettu padikkilla, kandathariyathavan kondathariyum.

literal_meaning: A wedding between a crow and a chicken.
figurative_meaning: A completely chaotic, mismatched, or absurd situation.
example: Aa projectil ellam kuzhapam aanu, kaakkakkum kozhikkum kallyaanam pole.

literal_meaning: Only those who have bitterness know the value of sweetness.
figurative_meaning: Only those who have suffered know the true value of happiness.
example: Daridryam anubhavichavarkke panathinte vila ariyoo, kaippullavane madhurathinte vilayariyu.

idiom: കാട്ടിലെ തടി തേവരുടെ ആന (Kaattile thadi thevarude aana)
literal_meaning: Timber from the forest, elephant belongs to the Lord.
figurative_meaning: Carelessly spending or destroying property that belongs to someone else.
example: Sarkaar panam avan dhoorthadikkunnu, kaattile thadi thevarude aana pole.

idiom: ചോദിക്കാൻ ആളില്ലെങ്കിൽ അമ്പലവാസി എന്തും ചെയ്യും (Chodikkan aalillengil ambalavaasi enthum cheyyum)
literal_meaning: If no one questions, the temple worker will do anything.
figurative_meaning: Without oversight or accountability, people will abuse their power.
example: Manager illatha neram avar paniyedukkilla, chodikkan aalillengil ambalavaasi enthum cheyyum.

idiom: താൻ കുഴിച്ച കുഴിയിൽ താൻ തന്നെ വീഴും (Thaan kuzhicha kuzhiyil thaan thanne veezhum)
literal_meaning: You will fall into the pit you dig.
figurative_meaning: Karma; if you plot against others, you will ruin yourself.
example: Avan vere oralude pani kalayaan sramichu pakshe avante pani poyi, thaan kuzhicha kuzhiyil thaan thanne veezhum.

idiom: നൂറു വട്ടം അറുത്താലും കൊതുകിന്റെ കാല് (Nooru vattam aruthalum kothukinte kaalu)
literal_meaning: Even if cut 100 times, a mosquito's leg remains small.
figurative_meaning: Something insignificant will remain insignificant no matter what you do.
example: Avanude businessil ethra maattangal varuthiyalum athu valuthaavilla, nooru vattam aruthalum kothukinte kaalu thanne.

literal_meaning: Like catching a tiger's tail.
figurative_meaning: Being caught in a dangerous situation where you can neither hold on nor let go.
example: Ee puthiya jobil aake prashnamanu, pulivaalu pidichathupole aayi.

literal_meaning: Do not cut a banana tree with a stick.
figurative_meaning: Do not do foolish things; use the right tools for the right job.
example: Avan ee periya project oru chinna tool vechu cheyyan sramikkunnu, vadiyeduthu vazha vettaruthu.

idiom: തല പോയാലും ചിരി മാറില്ല (Thala poyalum chiri maarilla)
literal_meaning: Even if the head is cut, the smile won't fade.
figurative_meaning: A deeply ingrained habit or characteristic persists until the very end.
example: Avan marikkuvolam jhooth parayum, thala poyalum chiri maarilla.

idiom: പാലം കടക്കുവോളം നാരായണ നാരായണ (Paalam kadakkuvolam Narayana Narayana)
literal_meaning: Praying Narayana until crossing the bridge.
figurative_meaning: Acting humble and devoted only as long as you are in danger or need help.
example: Avashyam theernappol avan enne marannu, paalam kadakkuvolam Narayana Narayana.

idiom: പത്തായത്തിൽ നെല്ലുണ്ടെങ്കിൽ എലി വയനാട്ടിൽ നിന്നും വരും (Pathayathil nellundengil eli wayanattil ninnum varum)
literal_meaning: If there is paddy in the granary, rats will come even from Wayanad.
figurative_meaning: If you are wealthy or successful, people will find you no matter where you are.
example: Avanu lottery adichappol ellavarum vannu, pathayathil nellundengil eli wayanattil ninnum varumallo.

idiom: വെള്ളത്തിൽ വരച്ച വര പോലെ (Vellathil varacha vara pole)
literal_meaning: Like a line drawn on water.
figurative_meaning: Something that disappears instantly; fleeting and impermanent.
example: Avarude sneham vellathil varacha vara poleyayi, udane maanju poyi.

literal_meaning: There is no god greater than the mother.
figurative_meaning: A mother is the supreme figure of love and reverence.
example: Amma parayunnathu kelkkanam, maathavinekkaal valiya daivamilla.

literal_meaning: Just because you close your eyes, it doesn't become dark.
figurative_meaning: Ignoring a problem does not make it go away.
example: Nee sathyam manassilakku, kannadachal iruttaavilla.

idiom: പെറ്റ തള്ളയ്ക്ക് അറിയാം പിള്ളയുടെ വേദന (Petta thallakku ariyaam pillayude vedana)
literal_meaning: Only the mother who gave birth knows the child's pain.
figurative_meaning: Only the person intimately involved in a situation truly understands the struggle.
example: Nammude prashnam namukke ariyoo, petta thallakku ariyaam pillayude vedana.

idiom: തേൻ എടുത്തവൻ കൈ നക്കും (Then eduthavan kai nakkum)
literal_meaning: He who takes the honey will lick his fingers.
figurative_meaning: People managing money or resources will naturally take a small cut for themselves.
example: Sarkaar udhyogasthar panam vangi, then eduthavan kai nakkumallo.

literal_meaning: Arrogance makes you lose touch with the ground.
figurative_meaning: When success goes to someone's head, they forget their humble beginnings.
example: Avanu ippol nalla ahankaram aanu, thalakkanam vannal tharayariyilla.

idiom: നാട് ഓടുമ്പോൾ നടുവേ ഓടണം (Naadu odumbol naduve odanam)
literal_meaning: When the village runs, you should run in the middle.
figurative_meaning: You should adapt to the customs and trends of the society you live in.
example: Ivide ellavarum inganeyanu cheyyunnathu, naadu odumbol naduve odanam.

literal_meaning: A wise man is respected everywhere.
figurative_meaning: Knowledge and talent will bring respect regardless of location.
example: Avanude budhi kaaranam avanu eppozhum velayundu, vidwanu evideyum sthaanam.

literal_meaning: Do not cut the branch you are sitting on.
figurative_meaning: Do not destroy the very thing that supports you.
example: Ninne sahayikkunna aale thettikkaruthu, irikkunna kombu murikkaruthu.

idiom: കൈ വിട്ട ആയുധം പോലെ (Kai vitta aayudham pole)
literal_meaning: Like a weapon that has left the hand.
figurative_meaning: Words once spoken or actions once taken cannot be reversed.
example: Vaakkukal sookshichu parayanam, kai vitta aayudham poleyanu.

literal_meaning: Sail according to the wind.
figurative_meaning: Adapt your actions according to the changing circumstances.
example: Market maarunnathinu anusarichu business maattanam, kaattinothu paaya virikkuka.

idiom: താൻ പാതി ദൈവം പാതി (Thaan paathi daivam paathi)
literal_meaning: Man does half, God does half.
figurative_meaning: You must put in the effort, and God will take care of the rest.
example: Nee padikkuka, baakki deivam nokkikkollum, thaan paathi daivam paathi.

idiom: പയ്യെ തിന്നാൽ പനയും തിന്നാം (Payye thinnal panayum thinnam)
literal_meaning: If you eat slowly, you can even eat a palm tree.
figurative_meaning: With patience and perseverance, you can achieve impossible things.
example: Ee valiya project padukke theerkkam, payye thinnal panayum thinnam.

idiom: മോങ്ങാനിരുന്ന നായയുടെ തലയിൽ തേങ്ങ വീണു (Mongaanirunna naayayude thalayil thenga veenu)
literal_meaning: A coconut fell on the head of a dog that was already about to howl.
figurative_meaning: Providing a ready excuse for someone who was already looking for a reason to complain.
example: Avanu officeil pokan madi aayirunnu appozha mazha vannathu, mongaanirunna naayayude thalayil thenga veenu.
